note: Public sources fetched for research: a weather forecast (model values), a satellite vegetation index and the official groundwater assessment. Not crop advice or a declaration.

weather.source: ECMWF IFS open-data forecast, via Open-Meteo
weather.measure: Daily reference evapotranspiration (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith, mm) and precipitation (mm) at a point inside each mandal. Days before today are the model's own recent runs, not station measurements.

vegetation.product: NOAA STAR Blended Vegetation Health Product (VIIRS), VCI, 4 km weekly
vegetation.weighting: Each 4 km cell weighted by its cropland share (ESA WorldCover 2021); a mandal with less than half a cell of cropland keeps the plain all-vegetation mean, and says so.
vegetation.classes: Manual for Drought Management 2020, Table 3.4: 60-100 normal, 40-60 moderate, 0-40 severe

cropland.source: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200, class 40 (cropland), read at about 330 m and counted per NOAA VHP 4 km cell
cropland.caveat: Cropland as seen in 2021 imagery, not this season's sowing; plantations and orchards count as tree cover.

assessment.source: Dynamic Ground Water Resources assessment (CGWB and the AP State Ground Water Department, GEC-2015 method), via INGRES
assessment.unitNote: Volumes in hectare-metres (1 ham = 10,000 m3). Stage of extraction = annual extraction / annual extractable resource. Categories: safe up to 70%, semi-critical 70-90%, critical 90-100%, over-exploited above 100%; saline where the groundwater is too salty to use.

soilCapacity.source: ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0: volumetric water content at 33 kPa (wv0033) and 1500 kPa (wv1500), mean predictions, 250 m
soilCapacity.method: Per depth interval: water at field capacity minus water at the wilting point (FAO-56 Eq. 82), averaged over the cells whose centre lies in the mandal, on a 0.01 degree grid.
soilCapacity.unit: mm of plant-available water per metre of soil
